ideas.name: 'Reserved-for-you' show-up engine: WhatsApp pass, plan-making, T-8 reconfirm, leak-proof seat ops
ideas.concept: Turn every registration into a held seat: instant auto-confirm, no general waitlist, a switch/transfer cancel flow and a WhatsApp cadence that reconfirms at T-8 but never releases a general-entry pass.
ideas.budget_split: BSP platform Rs 8,000 (Rs 2,000 x 4 months [WA-04]); utility messages Rs 5,700 (stretch volume x 6.5 sends x Rs 0.236 = (0.115 + 0.0846) x 1.18 GST [WA-01, WA-04]); marketing-category messages Rs 2,800 (T-3 win-back + day-1 friend link, about 2,500 x Rs 1.12); gate scanning kit (offline scanner on volunteer phones, 2 routers, printed fallback lists) Rs 2,500; contingency Rs 1,000. SMS fallback dropped (DLT registration alone costs Rs 11,800 [SMS-01]); email is the fallback.
ideas.dates: BSP live, templates approved and holdout randomiser on by Sun 3 Jan; live from registration day, Mon 4 Jan; T-30 Thu 11 Feb; first-year message Tue 2 Mar; T-8 reconfirm Fri 5 Mar; T-2 Thu 11 Mar (merged into T-1 if Eid moves); T-1 Fri 12 Mar; morning-of 13-14 Mar; holdout read by Fri 19 Mar.
ideas.contribution_math: Applied once to all 2,894.5 non-competition registrations, in sequence. Pre-engine visitors 2,148.2 (74.2%). Step 1, leak recovery: leakers = each line's net registrations x its 2025 leak rate = 250.8; recovered 43.2% (80% of interested, 100% of waitlisted, 10% of cancelled, weighted 29/88/183) = 108.3 passes x 68.75% show = +74.4. Step 2, reminders: confirmed residual no-shows 529.4 x 12.5% (half the RCT's 25% cut [SHOW-09]) x 85% treated = +56.2 (the holdout costs 9.9). Base +130.7. Stretch (100/100/30% recovery at 77% show; full RR 0.75): +135.3 + +142.5 = +277.8.
ideas.test_design: 15% holdout randomised by phone hash, squads as clusters (design effect 1.12). Holdout gets a plain pass (no ownership wording, no plan-making), no T-30, a NEUTRAL T-8 'Still coming? Y/N' poll with no reminder content and no seat release, and a T-1 route/safety message. Decision read: the T-8 YES-rate gap, treated (2,460) vs holdout (434). MDE at 80% power (one-sided 5%) is 6.3pp; the modelled check-in gap is 2.4pp (base) to 5.3pp (stretch), so the read is pre-registered as directional and the engine is never stopped on the gap alone. Second test: cancel-flow A/B (switch day or transfer to a friend, vs plain cancel) on passes saved per cancel request, about 226 requests in the season; read at Gate 3 (MDE about 17pp, directional).
kpis: T-8 YES rate, treated >= 75%; gap vs holdout >= 2pp (base) / >= 5pp (stretch)
ideas.leading_indicator: T-8 YES-rate gap (treated vs holdout) on Fri 5 Mar; before that, opt-out and plan-completion from Gate 1 and the cancel-flow save rate at Gate 3.

thresholds.scale: T-8 gap >= 5pp and opt-out <= 3%: add a day-2 nudge to day-1 no-shows and show the plan prompt to every treated registrant.
thresholds.change: Gap < 2pp, plan completion < 30%, opt-out 3-8% or cancel save < 10%: switch to the better wording, make the plan prompt one tap, drop T-30, make 'transfer to your squad' the default.
thresholds.stop: Opt-out > 8% on any send or Meta quality rating 'low' for 3 days: keep only the pass, T-1 and morning-of (two reminders beat one [SHOW-10]).

ideas.critical_variable: T-8 reconfirm gap and opt-out rate
ideas.biggest_risk: Message fatigue lowers the Meta quality rating, or reminders transfer weakly from health RCTs to a free fest.
ideas.early_success: Gate 1: opt-out <= 3%, 98% live pass within 48 h, plan completion >= 55%. Gate 4: treated YES >= 75% and >= 5pp above holdout.
ideas.early_failure: Opt-out > 5% on any send, quality rating 'low', plan completion < 30%, T-8 gap < 1pp.
ideas.action: Same day a channel's T-8 YES rate falls under 60%: nudge its squad leads (peer loop) and lower its show prior in the forecast; never cancel its passes.
ideas.dashboard_ai: Growth Center funnel ribbon (registered -> live pass -> reconfirmed -> checked in) by channel and arm; holdout gap with a 90% CI and an 'n too small' flag; opt-out alarm. Copilot answers 'how many front-zone seats can we release?' as (zone capacity - forecast check-ins) x 0.9 with the arithmetic shown, using counts only; any release batch is a create_task card a human approves [SDK-05].
ideas.dependencies_risks: Opt-in at registration; Meta template approval; utility classification (marketing costs 7.5x [WA-01]); the pass/QR build in the Growth Center. Risks: fatigue, Eid timing, first-years muted 3-9 Mar (messaged on Tue 2 Mar instead). Overlap: credited only with show-up uplift on registrations other ideas create, in a fixed order (leak recovery, then reminders on the confirmed residual). Capacity-limited sub-zones (pro-nite front zone, workshop halls, hackathon seats) release a seat only after an explicit 'No' or two unanswered prompts; general entry never releases.

ice.I_basis: base incremental visitors 130.7 / 35 (10 = about 350, a whole 2025 channel), floor 1
ice.C_basis: RCTs from health and voting [SHOW-09, SHOW-10, SHOW-14] plus exact 2025 leak counts; transfer to a free fest is the uncertainty
ice.E_basis: Rs 20K and one owner; general waitlist and pass release removed; one custom flow (switch/transfer/release-by-choice)

ideas.name: College club-charter grid + shared-bus pilot (double down on 2025's best channel)
ideas.concept: Scale 2025's best channel to 40 partner colleges (30 metro engineering, 10 OU-area degree and women's), each chartering 2-3 clubs that compete in a Club Cup ranked on verified check-ins.
ideas.budget_split: Acquisition Rs 64,000: kits and club co-hosted events Rs 54,000 (Rs 1,350 per partner), partner-code QR standees Rs 5,000, Club Cup Rs 5,000. Shared-bus pilot Rs 14,000: 4 bus-days x Rs 3,500 in the two densest corridors, each bus pooled across 2-3 neighbouring partners, justified on women's night-time access rather than CPV (zero base credit). Eligible for the reserve at Gate 2 (Wave C + a second co-hosted event at the top 20 partners).
ideas.dates: Shortlist frozen Sun 6 Dec; 25 MoUs by Sun 10 Jan plus 8 more by Mon 18 Jan; Wave A live Mon 18 Jan; 40 MoUs + 8 standbys by Sun 31 Jan; Wave B (+ Wave C) Mon 8 Feb; pre-events weekdays only (none 1-7 Feb, none on GATE weekends; at Inter exam-centre campuses none after 23 Feb); bus go/no-go Wed 3 Mar; manifests close Mon 8 Mar; buses run Sat 13 Mar.
ideas.contribution_math: Acquisition spend only: 450 x (64/31)^0.75 = 775.0 gross partner-code registrations; net 450 + 325.0 x 0.8 = 710.0; visitors 385 + 260.0 x (85.6% - 10pp) = 581.5, i.e. +196.5. Buses: 0 in the base. Stretch: cadence up to x1.10 = 852.5 gross, +243.3 visitors, plus the bus pilot +16.0 (160 riders x 10pp) = +259.3. Average CPV of the line Rs 110; marginal Rs 212 before the engine, Rs 201 with it. Operating target: 3.9 partner-code registrations per active partner-week over 200 partner-weeks (Wave A 20 x 6, Wave B 20 x 4; 1-7 Feb excluded). If the reserve goes to the grid it must add 440 gross registrations: Wave C (8 partners x 4 weeks at 3.9) gives 124, so the second co-hosted events at the top 20 partners must bring about 16 registrations each.
ideas.test_design: Matched-pair staggered rollout within corridor: the 24 partners signed by 10 Jan form 12 size-and-corridor pairs; one of each pair goes live 18 Jan, the other 8 Feb. Read registrations per 1,000 students from all sources at Gate 1; causal read = Wave A ahead in at least 9 of 12 pairs (one-sided sign test p = 0.073). CTWA excludes partner campuses until 8 Feb so the two tests do not confound. Bus pilot: rider vs non-rider show among the pooled partners (directional).
kpis: Active partners per week: 20 (from 18 Jan), 40 (from 8 Feb); the 1-7 Feb pause is exempt from alerts
Days since a partner's last registration: alert at 7
Wave A ahead in >= 9 of 12 pairs at Gate 1
Bus seats booked >= 40 per pooled bus by Wed 3 Mar
ideas.leading_indicator: Partner-code registrations per active partner-week, and the matched-pair sign test at Gate 1.

thresholds.scale: >= 4.5 registrations per partner-week and Wave A ahead in >= 9 of 12 pairs at Gate 2: the reserve funds Wave C (8 standbys) and a second co-hosted event at the top 20 partners.
thresholds.change: Below 3.3 per partner-week (85% of plan) for 2 weeks: swap the activation (club co-hosted mini-event instead of posters; switch IEEE charter to a dance or music club) and move volunteer hours to top-quartile partners. (Hold band: 3.3-4.5.)
thresholds.stop: A partner with < 1 registration a week for 2 consecutive active weeks is dropped and its campus handed to ambassadors. Grid projected CPV (accrual) > Rs 275 for 2 weeks freezes new MoUs. A bus with < 25 seats at T-10 is cancelled.

ideas.critical_variable: Active partners per week and registrations per partner-week
ideas.biggest_risk: Partners going dark (the 2025 weeks 8-10 stall) or autonomous colleges with their own mid-terms (e.g. NRCM 25-30 Jan [cal HYD-03]).
ideas.early_success: 25+ MoUs by 10 Jan; 18+ of Wave A's 20 active in week 1; >= 3.9 per partner-week; Wave A ahead in 9+ of 12 pairs.
ideas.early_failure: < 15 MoUs by 10 Jan; any partner with zero registrations for 7 days; < 2 per partner-week in the first two selling weeks.
ideas.action: Monday review re-ranks partners by registrations per partner-week; a dark partner gets a call within 24 h and a volunteer visit within 48 h.
ideas.dashboard_ai: Campaigns page: partner and corridor leaderboard, projected visitors from the engagement-adjusted show score; momentum-drop alert at 7 days of zero registrations (it would have flagged the 2025 stall in week 8). Copilot drafts each partner's weekly nudge from that partner's counts (pseudonymous IDs; names merged server-side after the model responds); pausing a partner is an update_campaign card a human approves.
ideas.dependencies_risks: Principal/HOD sign-offs before the breaks; partner calendars; parental-consent and liability clauses after the Malla Reddy incident [fest HYD-13]. Overlap: ambassadors are barred from partner colleges; partner code outranks squad, ambassador, paid and organic codes. The KPI counts all registrations from partner-college students, whatever the code, so precedence rules do not move it.

ice.I_basis: base incremental visitors 196.5 / 35 (10 = about 350, a whole 2025 channel), floor 1
ice.C_basis: Own 2025 data on the channel (85.6% show, 90.0% identified-to-registered); beta 0.75 assumed
ice.E_basis: 40 external sign-offs plus 8 standbys, parental-consent clauses, bus logistics

ideas.name: Verified-check-in peer loop: Squad Pass + ambassador league + day-1 friend link
ideas.concept: Make attendance a group decision: a Squad Pass at registration, a 60-ambassador league in non-partner colleges and a day-1 friend link, all rewarded only on verified check-ins.
ideas.budget_split: Squad rewards Rs 25,000 (Rs 100 per completed squad, about 250) + link build and leaderboard screens Rs 5,000; ambassador league Rs 42,000 (T-shirts, guest passes, top-10 stipends; certificates, letters and GCC interview fast-tracks in kind [CA-01, fest NAT-05]).
ideas.dates: Ambassadors recruited 7-20 Dec (outside the frozen shortlist); squad flow live with registration (4 Jan); squad A/B from Mon 18 Jan, decided at Gate 2 (or Gate 3 if extended); leaderboard paused 13-17 Jan and 1-7 Feb; friend link Sat 13 Mar 6 pm; rewards paid 15-25 Mar.
ideas.contribution_math: Base (no squad uplift assumed): referrals 350 x (30/19)^0.70 = 481.9 gross; net 455.5; +72.3 visitors at 78.6% - 10pp. Ambassadors held at Rs 42K: 0. Base +72.3; observed k = 0.198 (2025: 0.143). Stretch: season k 0.22 x 3,066.5 seeds = 674.6 gross, +178.1; ambassadors x1.15 +40.6; friend link +61.2 (day-1 visitors x 19% x 2 x 13% [REF-01] x 60% show); total +279.9.
ideas.test_design: Squad-first vs solo A/B, 50/50 from 18 Jan. Primary metric: 48-hour share rate (k is directional because it needs 7 days to mature). About 358 per arm by Gate 2 gives an MDE of 6.6pp on a 15% share rate (80% power); pre-committed rule: roll squad-first to 100% if the gap is >= 5pp at p < 0.1, otherwise extend to Gate 3 (747 per arm, MDE 4.6pp).
kpis: Duplicate or fake recruits per ambassador <= 5%
Day-2 new verified visitors per 100 day-1 messages >= 3 (stretch)
ideas.leading_indicator: 48-hour share rate in the squad A/B; ambassador activation at day 14.

thresholds.scale: Share-rate gap >= 5pp at p < 0.1 at Gate 2: squad-first becomes the default; fast-lane entry for squads fully reconfirmed by T-1.
thresholds.change: k 0.12-0.18 (below 90% of the base plan) or share rate 10-20%: move the share prompt into the plan-making 'who with' step, cut the minimum squad to 3, switch to zero-cash front-zone access. (Hold: k 0.18 or more.)
thresholds.stop: k < 0.12 after one change cycle (Gate 3): revert to a plain referral link and move unspent squad rewards (about Rs 15K) to the reserve. An ambassador with > 10% duplicates is disqualified; one inactive at day 14 is replaced.

ideas.critical_variable: Share rate x invites x invite conversion (k)
ideas.biggest_risk: Leaderboard fraud and inactive ambassadors; k below 2025.
ideas.early_success: Gate 1: share rate >= 25%, completion drop <= 2pp, >= 60% of ambassadors active.
ideas.early_failure: Share rate < 10%; squad-first k < 0.12; > 10% of an ambassador's recruits failing OTP or dedupe.
ideas.action: k reviewed twice a week and decomposed into share x invites x conversion; one change ships within 48 h.
ideas.dashboard_ai: Loop panel (k by seed source, college and week), squad funnel (formed -> fully reconfirmed -> arrived), ambassador league with fraud flags. Copilot sees pseudonymous squad and ambassador IDs plus counts only; it drafts nudge templates with placeholders and the server merges names after it responds. Disqualifications need human approval.
ideas.dependencies_risks: Depends on the engine's pass (the share moment) and person-level dedupe. Rewards: fast-lane for squads fully reconfirmed by T-1; front-zone access and the Rs 100-per-squad food combo unlock live once all members scan in; merch and letters paid after the event on verified check-ins. Friend-link registrants are a registrant source with their own show rate, not walk-ins.

ice.I_basis: base incremental visitors 72.3 / 35 (10 = about 350, a whole 2025 channel), floor 1
ice.C_basis: Own 2025 data for both channels; the squad uplift is gated, not assumed
ice.E_basis: One owner plus 60 ambassadors; needs clean person-level dedupe

ideas.name: Paid rebuilt: geo-tested Click-to-WhatsApp Reels + Telugu nano creators (shrink and fix)
ideas.concept: Cut paid and creators from Rs 1,52,000 to Rs 55,000 and rebuild the rest as geo-tested Click-to-WhatsApp Reels plus 4 Telugu nano creators, every lead landing in the engine.
ideas.budget_split: CTWA Rs 40,000: Rs 12,000 pilot 18-31 Jan + Rs 28,000 scale flight 8-27 Feb unless the pilot is above Rs 137 per registration (includes up to Rs 2,000 retargeting of unreconfirmed registrants). Creators Rs 15,000: 2 creators in the pilot (Rs 7,500); 2 more 8-21 Feb only if the pilot beats Rs 137 per registration (projected CPV under the Rs 275 stop), else that Rs 7,500 moves to the reserve. At the measured Rs 169 it does not, so the base moves it.
ideas.dates: Creator screening 4-15 Jan; pilot 18-31 Jan; no paid 1-7 Feb; decision Sun 7 Feb; scale 8-27 Feb; retargeting only after 27 Feb.
ideas.contribution_math: Base, capped at measured cost: CTWA min(680 x (40/93)^0.62 = 403.4, 40,000 / 110.2 = 362.9) = 362.9 registrations x 50% = 181.4 visitors (2025: 340); creators: the pilot reads Rs 168.6 per registration, above the Rs 137.5 gate, so only the Rs 7,500 pilot runs: 44.5 registrations x 50% = 22.2 (2025: 175) and Rs 7,500 joins the reserve. The cut is booked as its own line: -311.3 visitors while paid and creators spend falls from Rs 1,52,000 to Rs 47,500 (Rs 336 freed per visitor given up). This idea is credited only with the structural gain: base 0; stretch x1.5 registrations per rupee (CTWA Rs 73, creators Rs 112, so the creators' second round runs) = +113.0. Marginal CPV at plan: CTWA Rs 220, creators Rs 337 (before the engine), the highest of any line, hence capped and gated.
ideas.test_design: College-level geo test: 2-km geo-fences around 40 non-partner metro engineering colleges, 20 lit and 20 dark, stratified by corridor and size, partner campuses excluded until 8 Feb; read registrations per 1,000 seats. Directional unless the 90% CI excludes zero; 'no geo-lift' is not an automatic stop. Gate 2 decides on cost per registration plus the engagement-adjusted show score. Each creator ranked on cost per confirmed registration via a unique code.
kpis: CTWA cost per registration: <= Rs 115 hold (base Rs 110), <= Rs 73 stretch
Creators cost per registration: <= Rs 137 for a second round (measured Rs 169), <= Rs 112 stretch
ideas.leading_indicator: Weekly cost per registration by ad set and creator, with the show score of the registrants it buys.

thresholds.scale: CTWA <= Rs 73 per registration with show score >= 55% at Gate 2: full Rs 28K flight and eligibility for the reserve. (Hold band: Rs 74-115, which contains the base Rs 110.)
thresholds.change: CTWA Rs 116-137 per registration, or CTR down > 30% week on week: rotate creative within 72 h, shift to retargeting engagers, swap the weakest creator. Creators above Rs 137: no second round (Rs 7,500 to the reserve); reuse their content as CTWA creative.
thresholds.stop: CTWA > Rs 137 per registration (2025 average) for 2 consecutive weeks: pause and return the rest to the reserve. A creator > Rs 200 per registration gets no further posts.

ideas.critical_variable: Cost per registration and the show quality of paid registrants
ideas.biggest_risk: Creative fatigue (the 2025 week-10 collapse: 105 -> 35 registrations at flat Rs 14,400) and low-intent leads (2025 paid showed 50%).
ideas.early_success: Pilot CTWA <= Rs 110 per registration; creators <= Rs 137; show score >= 55%; lit colleges ahead of dark.
ideas.early_failure: Pilot CTWA > Rs 137; opt-out > 8%; registrations per Rs 1,000 down > 40% week on week at flat spend.
ideas.action: Budget moves within 48 h of a threshold; every rupee pulled goes to the reserve.
ideas.dashboard_ai: Daily cost per registration and projected CPV by ad set and creator; CTR-decay and momentum-drop alerts; geo-test chart. Copilot's simulate_budget_shift answers 'move Rs 10K from CTWA to the grid' on one consistent basis (both sides including the engine) and states the curve assumption; pausing or cutting budget needs human approval.
ideas.dependencies_risks: Depends on the engine's flow and on grid and peer content for retargeting pools. About 1 in 4 creator profiles fails an authenticity screen [INF-04]; the ad audience is about 70% male [MED-01], hence female-led creators. People first touched by peers stay credited to peers.

ice.I_basis: base incremental visitors 0.0 / 35 (10 = about 350, a whole 2025 channel), floor 1
ice.C_basis: The structural gain rests on vendor benchmarks [PAID-01, INF-04]; the base uses measured 2025 costs

ideas.name: Compete-to-attend: sponsor-gated team competitions (option bet)
ideas.concept: Three sponsor-funded team tracks (10-12 hour daytime AI hackathon, BGMI cup, cultural crew battles) where every team member gets a pass; run only if a prize sponsor signs.
ideas.budget_split: Unstop promotion Rs 6,000 [SHOW-28], prelim logistics Rs 6,000, trophies and certificates Rs 3,000. The Rs 2-3 lakh prize pool must be sponsor-funded; if no sponsor by Tue 12 Jan, the Rs 15,000 moves to the reserve.
ideas.owner: Nisha Rao (Creators/community), prelims hosted with Meera Iyer
ideas.dates: Sponsor pitch 1 Dec-11 Jan; go/no-go Tue 12 Jan; Unstop listings Mon 18 Jan; prelims 15-23 Feb (weekdays; before Inter exams at exam-centre campuses); registrations close Sat 27 Feb; finals 13-14 Mar.
ideas.contribution_math: Not in the base. Sponsor band: 50x3 + 32x4 + 24x6 = 422 participants x (1 - 40% overlap) x 80% show = +202.6, minus the grid visitors the Rs 15K would have bought through the reserve = +126.7 net. Stretch: 70x3 + 48x4 + 32x6 = 594 participants = +285.1. Cash CPV Rs 74; fully loaded with a Rs 2.5 lakh prize pool about Rs 1,308, which is why it only runs on sponsor money.
ideas.test_design: Pre-registered slot-fill gates (Tue 12 Jan sponsor, Sun 14 Feb fill) so sunk cost cannot keep a failing track alive. Incrementality check: share of competitors who are first-time registrants from non-partner colleges, plus a one-question 'would you have come without the competition?' survey, to sanity-check the 40% haircut.
kpis: Sponsor signed by Tue 12 Jan (prize pool >= Rs 1.5 lakh)
Team completion (every member holds a pass) >= 90%
ideas.leading_indicator: Sponsor signature on 12 Jan, then slot fill by track on 14 Feb.

thresholds.scale: >= 90% of slots filled by Sun 14 Feb: open 20% more slots and add supporter passes, within the 4,500 pass cap.
thresholds.change: One track < 30% while others fill: move promotion to faster tracks, push IEEE and E-cell circulars, add a college-vs-college bracket.
thresholds.stop: No sponsor by Tue 12 Jan: no competitions; Rs 15K to the reserve. All tracks < 30% on Sun 14 Feb: stop and move the unspent balance to the reserve.

ideas.critical_variable: Sponsor signing date and slot fill
ideas.biggest_risk: No prize sponsor; flagship-campus teams prioritising their own fests.
ideas.early_success: Sponsor signed by 12 Jan; >= 60% of slots filled by 14 Feb (30 / 19 / 14 teams); >= 40% non-partner teams.
ideas.early_failure: No sponsor or a pool < Rs 1 lakh by 12 Jan; < 30% of slots by 14 Feb; > 60% of teams already partner-coded.
ideas.action: The track owner reallocates promotion and hall slots weekly; the partner vs non-partner split of the shortfall decides who pushes circulars (grid volunteers or ambassadors).
ideas.dashboard_ai: Slot-fill tracker per track against the 12 Jan and 14 Feb gates; sponsor pipeline as tasks on the Execute page. Copilot drafts a sponsor ROI one-pager from aggregated counts; nudges to captains of incomplete teams are create_task cards a human approves.
ideas.dependencies_risks: Sponsor cash by 12 Jan; 6 partner campuses for prelims; venue halls (production). Competition codes take top attribution precedence, so a participant is never also credited to the grid or the peer loop.

Fri 18 Dec: VENUE AND DATE LOCK. HITEX deposit paid by the production sponsor, or pivot to the fallback with a different owner: G.M.C. Balayogi Indoor Stadium (Sports Authority of Telangana, 3,576-5,000) [cal HYD-20]. 13-14 Mar is then fixed; there is no later date switch.

Sun 3 Jan: BSP live, WhatsApp templates approved, holdout randomiser on (before registration opens).

Sun 17 Jan: GATE 0. Pass: at least 1,000 interest-list opt-ins and 295 registrations.

18 Jan: Wave A (20 partners: 12 randomised from matched pairs + 8 non-experimental early signers). CTWA Rs 12K pilot on the 40-college geo test (partner campuses excluded until 8 Feb). Creators' first round. Squad-first vs solo A/B. Engine holdout live.
Sun 31 Jan: GATE 1. 40 MoUs + 8 standby MoUs signed. Pacing 934 registrations. Wave A vs B sign test.
JNTUH II-IV mid-terms 1-6 Feb [cal HYD-01], GATE 6-7 Feb [cal HYD-07]: no campus pushes, no paid. Only the engine runs.

Thu 11 Feb: T-30 check for early registrants (its reply rate is the Gate 3 show signal).
Fri 12 Feb: CPPMS filing, 29 days ahead, under the 14-day route [cal HYD-26].
13-14 and 20-21 Feb: GATE weekends, no activations. Competition prelims 15-23 Feb (finished before Inter exams start 24 Feb at exam-centre campuses [cal HYD-08]).
Mon 22 Feb: GATE 3. Pacing 1,919. Cancel-flow A/B winner rolled out; squad decision if extended.
27 Feb: acquisition ends; competition registrations close.
Tue 2 Mar: first-years get their bus booking and reconfirm message before their mid-terms (3-9 Mar) [cal HYD-02].
Wed 3 Mar: bus go/no-go (T-10): run a shared bus only with 40+ seats across 2-3 neighbouring partners; cancel under 25.
Fri 5 Mar: T-8 RECONFIRM to every registrant (holdout gets a neutral Y/N poll). A missing reply never voids a pass. GATE 4: pacing 2,626; reconfirm rates recalibrate the show forecast.
Sat 6 Mar: Shivaratri [cal HYD-05]. Mon 8 Mar: bus manifests close (first-year seat block open to Thu 11 Mar).
Wed 10 Mar: Eid, no sends; Thu 11 Mar: 'following day' holiday [cal HYD-04]. T-2 on Thu 11 Mar, merged into T-1 if Eid moves to Thu 11.
Fri 12 Mar: T-1 with route, gate and the 11 pm last train [cal HYD-11].

Morning-of gate and route message. 4 QR lanes + 2 surge lanes 5-8 pm + manual exception desk. Occupancy from entry scans plus hourly clicker exit counts; walk-in lane closes at 300 a day or at 90% of the permit.
Day 1 at 6 pm: verified attendees get the 'bring one friend tomorrow' link. Pro-nite ends 9:45 pm (10 pm sound rule [cal HYD-27]); shuttle to HITEC City station until 10:45 pm, women-priority seats.

If SRH has an IPL home match at Uppal (Malkajgiri commissionerate [cal HYD-28]): end the pro-nite by 9:30 pm, run the shuttle to 10:30 pm, ask HMRL to extend service citing the IPL precedent [cal HYD-12]. No date switch.
Read the holdout, Wave A/B, squad, cancel-flow and geo tests. Pay ambassador, squad and Club Cup rewards on verified check-ins only (15-25 Mar). Write the 2028 priors file.

visitors_2025.basis: Unique verified external visitors: admitted and verified check-ins, deduplicated by stable ID

walkins_day1_2025.basis: Walk-ins present on day 1 (55 day-1 only + 25 both days)

confirmed_2025.basis: Registrations whose final status was confirmed (77.0% of them attended)

budget_2027.basis: 2027 marketing budget (task brief; equal to the 2025 revised budget)

weekly_regs_2025.basis: Registrations per ISO week 4-15 of 2025; the peak week is 354

peak_week_2025.basis: Largest weekly registration count in 2025 (ISO week 13)

leaks_2025.basis: Registrants without a live pass at event time: 29 never confirmed, 88 stuck on the waitlist, 183 cancelled. All showed at 0%
leaks_2025.source: [DS] CampusFest 2025 dataset: analysis/out/deep_dive.json, research/data_findings.md status_paths, show_by_final_status

paid_tranches_2025.basis: Paid Social: weeks 5-9 spent Rs 52.8K for 479 registrations; weeks 10-15 spent Rs 40.2K for 201
paid_tranches_2025.source: [DS] CampusFest 2025 dataset: analysis/out/deep_dive.json, research/data_findings.md weekly spend and registrations

funnel_2025.basis: 2025 reach chain summed across the seven campaigns

day_split_2025.basis: Unique visitors by day; 251 first entries in the busiest day-1 hour (11:00)
day_split_2025.source: [DS] CampusFest 2025 dataset: analysis/out/deep_dive.json, research/data_findings.md days, first_entry_by_hour

channels_2025.basis: Per first-touch campaign: spend, registrations, verified visitors, identified people and final-status leaks

cpr_paid_floor.basis: Paid's cheapest measured cost per registration: Rs 52,800 / 479 (2025 weeks 5-9). The 2027 paid line is never modelled cheaper than this
cpr_paid_floor.source: [DS] CampusFest 2025 dataset: analysis/out/deep_dive.json, research/data_findings.md weekly paid data

cpr_creators.basis: Creators' 2025 average cost per registration: Rs 59,000 / 350. Their weekly response was flat and lagged (first Rs 24.4K bought 113 at Rs 216, the rest 237 at Rs 146), so they are modelled linear (beta 1.0)
cpr_creators.source: [DS] CampusFest 2025 dataset: analysis/out/deep_dive.json, research/data_findings.md weekly creator data

beta_ctwa_estimate.basis: ln(680/479) / ln(93/52.8) = 0.62. Estimated from cumulative 2025 spend tranches, so it is confounded with creative fatigue and lag; the CTWA geo test replaces it

beta_grid.basis: Partner output scales with partners and co-hosted events, slightly less than linearly
beta_grid.source: Judgement; tested by the matched-pair Wave A/B

beta_referrals.basis: Referral rewards scale with squads formed
beta_referrals.source: Judgement; tested by the squad A/B

beta_ambassadors.basis: Ambassador output scales with headcount and rewards

beta_community.basis: A fixed set of groups (IEEE section, Student Tribe, r/hyderabad), so extra money buys little

beta_organic.basis: Organic mostly captures demand other channels create; first-touch credit overstates it

beta_creators.basis: Linear at the measured Rs 169 per registration (audit fix: the borrowed paid beta was contradicted by the data)

haircut.basis: Share of registrations above a channel's 2025 volume that would have come through another channel anyway (first-touch attribution is not incremental)
haircut.source: Judgement; tested by Wave A/B and the geo test

haircut_competitions.basis: Competitors overlap heavily with partner and ambassador networks
haircut_competitions.source: Judgement; checked by the non-partner share of teams

quality_haircut.basis: Registrants above a channel's 2025 volume show 10pp below its 2025 rate (newer colleges, weaker ties; distance costs 1.55-12pp per mile [SHOW-17])

recovery_base.basis: Instant auto-confirm removes the 'interested' limbo (80%); with no general waitlist under the 4,500 pass cap every waitlisted registrant holds a pass (100%); the switch/transfer cancel flow saves 10% of the 183 who still cancelled (below the 16.4% the 2025 win-back already achieved on the first pass)
recovery_base.source: [DS] CampusFest 2025 dataset: analysis/out/deep_dive.json, research/data_findings.md leak counts; audit check 2 (waitlist recovery 100%)

recovery_stretch.basis: Stretch: cancel-flow save rate 30% (must be shown by the cancel-flow A/B at Gate 3)

recovered_show_base.basis: A recovered pass shows like an average 2025 registrant (1,925 / 2,800 = 68.75%), not like a confirmed one (77%)

recovered_show_stretch.basis: Stretch: a recovered pass shows like a 2025 confirmed registrant (1,925 / 2,500 = 77.0%)

rct_rr_noshow.basis: Text reminders cut no-shows to 0.75x (15% vs 21%) in a meta-analysis of RCTs

reminder_transfer_base.basis: Base keeps half the RCT effect (health appointments to a free student fest); plan-making and ownership wording get no extra credit

reminder_cut_stretch.basis: Stretch takes the full RCT effect (no-shows x 0.75); no extra credit for plan-making

treated_share.basis: 15% randomised holdout gets a plain pass, no plan-making, no T-30, a neutral T-8 Y/N poll and a T-1 safety/route message only

show_cap.basis: Median show rate of large PAID events; used only as a hard upper cap on registrant show-up

show_free_median.basis: Median show rate of large FREE events (24% no-show); PheedLoop advises planning for 70%

walkin_ratio_2025.basis: 125 / 1,925 = 6.5% of registered visitors; used in the stretch only

walkin_cap_per_day.basis: Gate-registration lane closes at 300 a day

friend_link.basis: Day-1 6 pm 'bring one friend tomorrow' link (stretch only): 19% share, about 2 shares each, 13% of friends register [REF-01]; 60% of those come on day 2 (assumption)

bus_pilot.basis: 4 shared bus-days (2-3 neighbouring partners each) x 40 riders; riders show 10pp more (distance costs 1.55-12pp per mile [SHOW-17]). Zero credit in the base; stretch only
bus_pilot.source: [SHOW-17] plus judgement; Rs 3,500 top-up is unsourced (3 quotes to be taken)

grid_cadence_stretch.basis: Up to x1.10: an always-on cadence recovers the 2025 stall (weeks 8-10 gave 29 registrations vs 78 at the weeks 6-7 run rate: 49 of 450 = 10.9%). Part of that was probably deferred, not lost
grid_cadence_stretch.source: [DS] CampusFest 2025 dataset: analysis/out/deep_dive.json, research/data_findings.md weekly partnership data

ambassador_league_stretch.basis: League paid on verified check-ins lifts ambassador output by 15%

paid_structural_stretch.basis: CTWA Reels and nano creators deliver 1.5x registrations per rupee vs measured 2025 cost (CTWA Rs 73, creators Rs 112 per registration). Reels CPM is about 1/3 of Feed [PAID-01]; CTWA skips the landing page where 2025 paid lost 78%; free 7-day window [WA-03]; regional micro-creators get 2-3x engagement [INF-04]
paid_structural_stretch.source: [PAID-01, WA-03, INF-04]; gated on the pilot

squad_k_stretch.basis: Season k (referred registrations per seed registration) 0.22 vs 0.143 in 2025 (350 / 2,450). Needs post-rollout k of at least 0.23 after the squad-first A/B

competitions.basis: Daytime AI hackathon (teams of 3), BGMI cup (4), cultural crews (6). 80% show (engaged 2025 registrants showed 79.4%). Runs only if a prize sponsor signs by Tue 12 Jan
competitions.source: [DS] CampusFest 2025 dataset: analysis/out/deep_dive.json, research/data_findings.md engagement; [fest HYD-02, HYD-06, SHOW-28]

value.line: Show-up engine: WhatsApp pass, plan-making, T-8 reconfirm, leak-proof seat ops
Club-charter grid: acquisition (40 partners: kits and co-hosted events Rs 54K, QR standees Rs 5K, Club Cup Rs 5K)
Shared college-bus pilot: 4 bus-days x Rs 3,500, 2-3 neighbouring partners per bus (zero base credit)
Squad Pass: Rs 100 per completed squad (about 250) + link build and leaderboard Rs 5K
Ambassador league: 60 ambassadors, rewards paid on verified check-ins
CTWA Reels: Rs 12K pilot (18-31 Jan) + Rs 28K scale flight (8-27 Feb, gated; includes up to Rs 2K retargeting)
Telugu nano creators: Rs 7.5K pilot + Rs 7.5K second round only if the pilot beats Rs 137 per registration (else to the reserve)
Competition operations (Unstop Rs 6K, prelims Rs 6K, trophies Rs 3K); moves to the reserve if no prize sponsor by Tue 12 Jan
Community groups (IEEE Hyderabad Section, Student Tribe, r/hyderabad AMA with moderator approval)
Performance reserve, released Mon 8 Feb at Gate 2 to the eligible line with the lowest measured marginal CPV

budget_lines.basis: Rs 3,00,000 split. Changes vs the panel: buses Rs 35K -> Rs 14K pilot; grid acquisition Rs 50K -> Rs 64K; organic Rs 10K -> Rs 14K; community Rs 15K -> Rs 16K; ambassadors Rs 40K -> Rs 42K (each restored where its marginal CPV below the 2025 level beats the grid's)

paid_next_visitor_cpv.basis: Rs 110 / 50% show = Rs 220: what one more visitor costs from a paid extension at 2025's best tranche. A line must beat it at the margin to receive the reserve ahead of paid

universal_stop_cpv.basis: No line runs at a projected CPV above Rs 275 (worse than 2025 paid's Rs 274) for 2 consecutive weeks; the reserve is never spent above it (it funds show-up operations instead)
universal_stop_cpv.source: [DS] CampusFest 2025 dataset: analysis/out/deep_dive.json, research/data_findings.md paid CPV Rs 274

ctwa_stop_cpr.basis: 2025 paid average cost per registration (Rs 93,000 / 680 = Rs 137). The Rs 28K scale flight runs unless the pilot is above it

creator_second_round_cpr.basis: Rs 275 x 50% show = Rs 137.5 per registration. The creators' second Rs 7.5K runs only if the pilot beats it; at the measured Rs 169 it does not, so the base moves it to the reserve

floor_definition.basis: FLOOR = base with (1) every acquisition curve, including the reserve's receiving line, delivering registrations / 1.15 (cost per registration 15% worse than 2025); (2) the show-up engine at half strength (leak recovery and reminder effect both halved); (3) no sponsor; (4) walk-ins flat at 125

eid_long_weekend.basis: Eid (Wed 10 Mar) + 'following day' holiday (Thu 11 Mar) [cal HYD-04] + second Saturday: if 30% of registrants are hostellers and their show-up drops 10pp

shuttle_cost_if_unsponsored.basis: HITEX to HITEC City station loop, 2 hired buses x 2 evenings x Rs 4,500; drawn from the reserve only if no shuttle sponsor by Fri 5 Feb

reach_frequency.basis: Average exposures per reached student; reach is a derived requirement, not a driver

priority_pool.basis: P1 = 1,07,218 intake [mkt HYD-08] x 85% fill [mkt HYD-10] x 4 years x 61% metro share [mkt HYD-11]; P2 = 99,242 OU-area degree seats filled [mkt HYD-12] x 3 years. Both assume average-sized metro colleges

t8_yes_rate_prior.basis: Expected T-8 YES rate, used only to size the holdout MDE

pacing_weights.basis: Each line's registrations spread over the weeks it is active (Sankranti quiet 13-17 Jan, exam pause 1-7 Feb, GATE weekends, 7-day identified-to-registered lag [DS])

engine.C_basis: RCTs from health and voting [SHOW-09, SHOW-10, SHOW-14] plus exact 2025 leak counts; transfer to a free fest is the uncertainty
engine.E_basis: Rs 20K and one owner; general waitlist and pass release removed; one custom flow (switch/transfer/release-by-choice)

grid.C_basis: Own 2025 data on the channel (85.6% show, 90.0% identified-to-registered); beta 0.75 assumed
grid.E_basis: 40 external sign-offs plus 8 standbys, parental-consent clauses, bus logistics

peer.C_basis: Own 2025 data for both channels; the squad uplift is gated, not assumed
peer.E_basis: One owner plus 60 ambassadors; needs clean person-level dedupe

paid.C_basis: The structural gain rests on vendor benchmarks [PAID-01, INF-04]; the base uses measured 2025 costs

compete.C_basis: No 2025 data; analogues measure participation, not verified show [fest HYD-02, HYD-06]
compete.E_basis: Needs a prize sponsor, judges and multi-team operations

ice_confidence_ease.basis: Anchored scales: C 9 = RCT plus own data on the same mechanism, 8 = own channel data or RCTs plus own leak counts, 6 = own data plus vendor benchmarks, 4-5 = external analogues or benchmarks only. E 9 = Rs 20K or less, one owner, configuration only; 7 = internal build plus volunteers; 5 = many external sign-offs; 4 = sponsor plus multi-team ops
